title: Code
covers: Source code, scripts, configuration and tests handed to a reviewer or the next developer.

stakeholders.who: The next developer who has to change this code
cares_about: understanding why it works this way
changing it without breaking something else
would_notice: names like data2, tmp or handleStuff
a second way of doing something the codebase already does
a function too long to hold in your head
no test to tell them they broke it

stakeholders.who: The code reviewer reading the diff
cares_about: a diff that only does what the task needed
a clean lint and type check
would_notice: a TODO the release depends on
a test that only covers the happy path

stakeholders.who: Whoever runs the code and gets the alert when it fails
would_notice: an empty catch that hides a failure
a key or token in a log line

first_ten_seconds: Read git diff --stat: does the list of files match the task, with nothing unrelated?
Open the main changed file: can you tell from names alone what each function does?
Find the test for the new behaviour: does it exist, and does it test a failure path too?

checks.claim: The diff holds only what the task needed: no commented-out code, stray debug prints, unrelated reformatting or leftover experiments.
checks.how_to_inspect: Read git diff from top to bottom; search the added lines for console.log, print(, debugger and commented-out blocks.
checks.evidence_required: The git diff --stat and the search over the added lines.

source.quote: no dead or commented-out code left behind

checks.claim: No TODO, FIXME or 'temporary' hack that the release depends on.
checks.how_to_inspect: Search the added lines for TODO, FIXME, HACK, XXX and temporary; each hit is fixed or has an owner and a reason.
checks.evidence_required: The search command and its output (zero hits, or each hit fixed).

checks.claim: Lint and type check are clean where the project has them, without new disable comments.
checks.how_to_inspect: Run the project's lint and typecheck commands; search the diff for eslint-disable, @ts-ignore, noqa and type: ignore.
checks.evidence_required: The commands with their exit codes and the search output.

source.quote: those tests plus typecheck/lint where the project has them

checks.claim: New behaviour has a test that would fail without the change, including at least one failure or edge path.
checks.how_to_inspect: Read the new tests, then break the change on purpose (or check out the old code) and confirm a test goes red.
checks.evidence_required: The test command output and the red run on the broken or old code.

source.quote: Tests — does new behavior have a real test

checks.claim: A bug fix changes the cause, not the symptom, and carries a regression test proven red on the old code.
checks.how_to_inspect: Write the root cause in one sentence and run the regression test against the commit before the fix.
checks.evidence_required: The root-cause sentence and the red-then-green test runs (N/A when the change is not a bug fix).

source.section: 2. Sloppy / quality complaints, by deliverable type
source.quote: Fix at the cause, add a regression test, record the lesson.

checks.claim: Every boundary the change touches handles errors with context: no empty catch, no failure silently turned into null or an empty list.
checks.how_to_inspect: Search the diff for catch blocks, .catch(, except: and fallback values; read what each one does with the error.
checks.evidence_required: The list of handlers and what each one reports.

source.quote: no empty catch blocks or errors turned into null/[] without context

checks.claim: Input from users, files, the network or the command line is validated where it enters, before it reaches HTML, a query or a shell.
checks.how_to_inspect: Trace each new input to its first use and feed one malformed value through a test or a manual run.
checks.evidence_required: The input list with where each is validated, and the malformed-input result.

source.quote: User input is validated at the boundary before use

checks.claim: No secret, key or token in source, logs, fixtures or commits; secrets come from env with placeholders in .env.example.
checks.how_to_inspect: Search the diff and new fixtures for key, token, secret, password and long random strings; check what the new log lines print.
checks.evidence_required: The search command and its output (zero hits, or each hit fixed).

source.quote: No secret, key, or token appears in source, logs, or committed files.

checks.claim: The change uses the patterns the codebase already has instead of adding a parallel way of doing the same thing.
checks.how_to_inspect: Search the codebase for an existing helper, module or convention that does what the new code does.
checks.evidence_required: The search and either the reuse made or why the existing pattern did not fit.

source.quote: No parallel or duplicate pattern was introduced where an established one already existed in the codebase.

checks.claim: Names say what things are, and functions and files stay within the project's own size conventions.
checks.how_to_inspect: Read the names of every new function and variable out of context; compare function and file length with the project norm.
checks.evidence_required: The names renamed and any function or file split.

source.quote: Naming, structure, and file size stay within this project's own conventions

checks.claim: Comments explain why, not what, and no comment contradicts the code it sits on.
checks.how_to_inspect: Read every comment next to the code it describes, including comments the change made stale.

source.rationale: A stale comment misleads the next developer faster than no comment at all.

checks.claim: Log and error messages name what failed, with an id or input that lets the operator find it, and without personal data.
checks.how_to_inspect: Trigger one failure and read the resulting log line as someone who did not write the code.
checks.evidence_required: The log line produced by the failure.

source.rationale: The operator reads the log without the author present; a bare 'something went wrong' turns a short fix into a long hunt.

common_sloppy_defects.symptom: console.log('here'), print statements or a commented-out old version in the diff
catch (e) {} or a failure turned into [] so the caller thinks there was simply no data
every test passes valid input; nothing tests the error branch the change added
an extra if-check around the crash site while the bad value is still produced upstream
new @ts-ignore, eslint-disable or noqa lines instead of fixing the warning
hundreds of whitespace changes that hide the three lines that matter
